appearance: A tiny being with a humanoid head, torso and arms and the wings, antennae and legs of a cricket. It has light blue skin, forest-green hair and hairy brown legs, and stands about a foot and a half tall.
behavior: Cheerful pranksters with no fear of bigger creatures, fond of stealing food, collapsing tents and throwing their voices to make objects talk. By sprite standards they are fierce, attacking fearlessly with bow and dagger.
appearanceGreenbound: The grig's cricket legs have turned to stiff, jointed twigs and its wings to veined, translucent leaves that buzz when it leaps. Its blue skin has roughened to green-flecked bark and a tuft of moss has taken the place of its hair.
note: Fey, so never a wild shape form. The summon nature's ally IX grig carries the fiddle (one grig in each band has one). Sprite is the Monster Manual's family heading for grig, nixie and pixie, not a separate creature; sprites share a +2 racial bonus on Search, Spot and Listen, already counted in the printed skills. Also reachable through Summon Fey (Kingdoms of Kalamar p.188, Drd 1, scalable).

name: Dire Bear
specialAttacks: improved grab (Ex -- must hit with a claw attack, free action grapple with no attack of opportunity)
skills: Listen +10, Spot +10, Swim +13
appearance: A hulking bear with heavy bony brow ridges, claws like sickles, and a cold, piercing, destructive gleam in its eyes. It runs about 12 feet long and weighs as much as 8,000 pounds.
behavior: It usually leaves creatures alone if they keep clear, but defends a kill or food source aggressively and will tear apart anything that might be edible. It fights by ripping with its claws.
appearanceGreenbound: The dire bear's shaggy coat has become thick, rough bark with moss packed into every crevice, and its sickle claws are hardened thorns. Roots trail from its paws and a crown of leafy twigs rises along its spine.

name: Elephant
specialAttacks: trample (Ex -- 2d8+15, Reflex half DC 25)
skills: Listen +12, Spot +10
appearance: A massive herbivore of tropical lands. The statistics describe an African elephant; Indian elephants are slightly weaker (Str 28) but easier to train (Wis 15), and the same block can stand in for mammoths and mastodons.
behavior: Unpredictable creatures, though sometimes used as mounts or beasts of burden. They tend to charge anything that threatens them.
appearanceGreenbound: The elephant's wrinkled hide has turned to deep-grooved bark, its tusks to pale knotted wood, and its ears to broad, rustling leaves. Vines coil about its legs and its eyes gleam from beneath a mossy brow.
note: The printed full attack is either slam plus two stamps, or the gore alone; both gore and slam are listed as primary attacks.

name: Girallon
specialAttacks: rend (Ex -- a girallon that hits with two or more claw attacks latches on and tears flesh for an automatic extra 2d4+9 damage)
skills: Climb +14 (+8 racial bonus, can take 10 while rushed or threatened), Move Silently +8, Spot +6
appearance: An albino gorilla with four arms, razor-sharp teeth and long claws, standing about 8 feet tall with thick white fur and weighing around 800 pounds. On the ground it walks on its legs and lower arms.
behavior: Savage, aggressive and highly territorial, it attacks anything that enters its range, even other girallons. It likes to lie hidden in branches or leaf litter with only its nose showing, charge when it spots or smells prey, and carry off anything small enough before the victim's friends can respond.
appearanceGreenbound: The girallon's white fur has become pale, shaggy moss over a body of hard, ridged wood, and its four arms end in claws like splintered branches. Leafy shoots crown its head and its eyes glow a dull green.
note: The printed stat block gives rend as 2d4+9 (1.5 x Str 22); the combat text prints 2d4+12. The stat block value is used. Toughness is taken twice.

name: Megaraptor
specialAttacks: pounce (Ex -- a charge allows a full attack)
skills: Hide +5, Jump +27, Listen +12, Spot +12, Survival +12 (+8 racial bonus on Hide, Jump, Listen, Spot and Survival)
appearance: A larger version of the deinonychus, standing about 12 feet tall and 24 feet long, with the same look, habits and abilities.
behavior: It hunts like its smaller cousin, pouncing on prey with a full attack.
appearanceGreenbound: The megaraptor's scales have become overlapping strips of green bark and its clawed feet knobbed roots. A fringe of leaves runs along its spine and tail, and its toothy jaws are lined with thorn-sharp splinters.

name: Octopus, Giant
specialAttacks: improved grab (Ex -- must hit an opponent of any size with a tentacle, free action grapple with no attack of opportunity; a won grapple check establishes a hold and allows constrict)
constrict (Ex -- 2d8+6 damage on a successful grapple check)
specialQualities: ink cloud (Ex -- once per minute as a free action, a 20-ft. cube of jet-black ink giving total concealment)
jet (Ex -- once per round as a full-round action, jets backward 200 ft. in a straight line without provoking attacks of opportunity)
skills: Escape Artist +12, Hide +12, Listen +4, Spot +6, Swim +13 (+4 Hide from color change, +10 Escape Artist from contorting, +8 racial on Swim checks for special actions or hazards; can take 10 and run while swimming)
appearance: An aggressive, territorial hunter with arms 10 feet or more long, their undersides studded with barbs and sharp-edged suckers.
behavior: It seizes prey with its tentacles and crushes it, and escapes losing fights behind an ink cloud and a backward jet.
appearanceGreenbound: The giant octopus's skin has become rough green bark, ridged and knotted, and its tentacles thick, supple vines tipped with thorns instead of suckers. Mossy tufts and leaves float around its mantle.
note: May be summoned only into an aquatic or watery environment.

name: Whale, Baleen
specialQualities: blindsight 120 ft. (a silence spell negates it and leaves the whale with human-quality vision)
hold breath (Ex -- 8 x its Con score in rounds, 176, before risking drowning)
skills: Listen +15, Spot +14, Swim +20 (+4 racial bonus on Listen and Spot, lost if blindsight is negated; +8 racial on Swim checks for special actions or hazards, can take 10 and run while swimming)
appearance: A plankton-feeding whale of 30 to 60 feet, such as a gray, humpback or right whale.
behavior: Surprisingly gentle: if harassed or provoked it is as likely to flee as to retaliate.
appearanceGreenbound: The baleen whale's skin has hardened into thick, barnacle-like bark crusted with moss, its fins into broad leafy paddles. Its dark eyes gleam beneath a brow of knotted wood.
note: May be summoned only into an aquatic or watery environment. Toughness is taken twice.

name: Salamander, Average
specialAttacks: constrict (Ex -- automatic tail slap damage, including fire, on a successful grapple check: 2d6+1 plus 1d6 fire)
heat (Ex -- its touch deals extra fire damage (1d6) and its metallic weapons conduct the same heat)
improved grab (Ex -- must hit a creature up to one size larger with its tail slap, free action grapple; a won grapple check establishes a hold and allows constrict)
specialQualities: damage reduction 10/magic (its natural weapons count as magic)
skills: Bluff +11, Craft (blacksmithing) +19 (+4 racial), Diplomacy +3, Disguise +1 (+3 acting), Hide +11, Intimidate +3, Listen +8, Move Silently +11, Search +12, Spot +8
appearance: A muscular humanoid upper body on a serpentine lower body covered in red and black scales, with flame-shaped spines on its head, arms and back. Medium-sized, with a reach of 10 feet with its tail.
behavior: Salamanders reproduce asexually, each producing a single larva every ten years and incubating it in fire pits. Average salamanders and flamebrothers are separate species; nobles rise from the ranks of the average. Bloodthirsty and sadistic, they favor spears heated red-hot by their own bodies, attack the apparently strongest foe first, and save weaker enemies for slow torment.
appearanceGreenbound: The salamander's scales have turned to blackened, cracked bark with ember-glowing seams, and the flame spines to licks of smoldering twigs. Its serpentine body ends in a root-like tail that smokes faintly.
note: Salamanders have Multiattack despite lacking the usual three natural weapons. The spear's extra fire damage is 1d6.

name: Xorn, Average
specialQualities: all-around vision (+4 racial bonus on Spot and Search checks; can't be flanked)
skills: Hide +10, Intimidate +10, Knowledge (dungeoneering) +10, Listen +10, Move Silently +10, Search +10, Spot +10, Survival +10 (+12 following tracks or underground)
appearance: A wide body of pebbly, stonelike material with a large powerful mouth on top of its head and three long, taloned arms placed symmetrically around it. Between the arms sit large stone-lidded eyes that see in every direction, over three short legs.
behavior: A scavenger from the Plane of Earth that does not hunt fleshly beings, since it can't digest meat, but pursues anyone carrying precious metals or minerals. It likes to wait just under a stone surface until a foe comes within reach.
appearanceGreenbound: The xorn's pebbled body has taken on the texture of rough bark with moss filling its seams, and its three arms have become thick, root-like limbs ending in thorn claws. Small leafy shoots grow between its stone-lidded eyes.

name: Pixie (no special arrows)
specialAttacks: spell-like abilities (caster level 8th, Cha-based DCs): 1/day -- lesser confusion (DC 14), dancing lights, detect chaos, detect good, detect evil, detect law, detect thoughts (DC 15), dispel magic, entangle (DC 14), permanent image (DC 19, visual and auditory only), polymorph (self only)
specialQualities: greater invisibility (Su -- constant, remains invisible when attacking, can suppress or resume as a free action)
skills: Bluff +7, Concentration +4, Escape Artist +8, Hide +8, Listen +8, Move Silently +8, Ride +8, Search +9, Sense Motive +6, Spot +8
appearance: A very small elf, about two and a half feet tall, with longer ears and gossamer wings, usually in bright clothing with a cap and curl-toed shoes.
behavior: Merry pranksters who love to lead travelers astray and tease the greedy with treasure they don't covet. They turn fierce against evil creatures and intruders, using invisibility and their other tricks to harass and drive them off.
appearanceGreenbound: The pixie's wings have become pale, veined leaves, and its skin and cap have taken on the grain and color of pale wood and curled bark. Tiny buds and tendrils sprout along its arms and ears, and it glows faintly green.
note: Fey, so never a wild shape form. The summon nature's ally VI pixie: no special arrows and cannot cast Otto's irresistible dance. Also reachable through Summon Fey (Kingdoms of Kalamar p.188, Drd 1, scalable).

name: Arrowhawk, Elder
specialAttacks: electricity ray (ranged touch +19, 2d8 electricity, 50-ft. range, usable once per round)
specialQualities: immunity to acid, electricity, and poison
skills: Diplomacy +3, Escape Artist +23, Knowledge (the planes) +18, Listen +21, Move Silently +23, Search +18, Sense Motive +19, Spot +21, Survival +19 (+21 following tracks, +21 Plane of Air), Use Rope +5 (+7 involving bindings)
appearance: An elder arrowhawk is a long, snakelike creature about 20 feet from beak to tail, with a 30-foot wingspan and a weight around 800 pounds, flying on two pairs of feathered wings in any direction without landing.
behavior: Extremely territorial and always hungry, it attacks almost any creature it meets, either for food or to drive off a rival. Its main weapon is an electricity ray fired from the tail. It is not usually talkative, but speaks Auran.
appearanceGreenbound: The elder arrowhawk's scales have thickened into layered bark with mossy seams and its wing feathers into broad, rustling leaves. Its beak has turned to a hard woody hook and a spray of thorny vines streams from its tail.

name: Dire Tiger
specialAttacks: improved grab (Ex -- must hit with its bite, free action grapple with no attack of opportunity; on a won grapple check it establishes a hold and can rake)
pounce (Ex -- a charge allows a full attack, including two rake attacks)
rake (Ex -- +18 melee, 2d4+4)
skills: Hide +7 (+4 racial bonus on Hide and Move Silently, Hide +8 more in tall grass or heavy undergrowth), Jump +14, Listen +6, Move Silently +11, Spot +7, Swim +10
appearance: An immense, monstrous cat almost as tall at the shoulder as a human, with a long body, bold stripes and paws the size of bucklers. It can reach over 12 feet long and weigh up to 6,000 pounds.
behavior: It preys on nearly anything that moves, patiently stalking a meal and striking when the creature lets its guard down: it runs at the prey, leaps, claws and bites, and rakes with its rear claws.
appearanceGreenbound: The dire tiger's stripes have become bold bands of dark and pale bark over a body of flexible wood, and its claws are curved thorns. Its ears are broad leaves and tendrils of ivy trail along its flanks.

name: Djinni
specialAttacks: air mastery (Ex -- airborne creatures take -1 on attack and damage rolls against it)

spell-like abilities (caster level 20th, Cha-based DCs): at will -- invisibility (self only); 1/day -- create food and water, create wine, major creation (vegetable matter permanent), persistent image (DC 17), wind walk; once per day can assume gaseous form for up to 1 hour

whirlwind (Su -- once every 10 minutes, up to 7 rounds; a creature touching it makes a DC 20 Reflex save or takes 3d6, then a second DC 20 Reflex save or is held aloft, taking 1d8 per round, and flying creatures get a DC 20 save each round to escape)
specialQualities: plane shift (Sp -- can enter any Elemental Plane, the Astral Plane or the Material Plane, carrying itself and up to eight other creatures who link hands with it; as the spell, caster level 13th)
skills: Appraise +12, Concentration +12, Craft (any one) +12, Diplomacy +4, Escape Artist +14, Knowledge (any one) +12, Listen +12, Move Silently +14, Sense Motive +12, Spellcraft +12, Spot +12, Use Rope +4 (+6 with bindings)
appearance: A well-formed human figure with a dark complexion, nearly twice as tall as a man, about 10 and a half feet and 1,000 pounds.
behavior: Djinn are genies of the Plane of Air who live on floating islands of earth and rock, ruled by local sheiks within a caliph's realm. They disdain physical combat and prefer magic and aerial tactics; one that is losing takes flight and becomes a whirlwind to harass pursuers. Djinn speak Auran, Celestial, Common and Ignan.
appearanceGreenbound: The djinni's skin has the grain and texture of dark polished wood, with green shoots spiraling from its arms and a crown of fresh leaves. Its eyes glow a soft green and its lower body swirls like a tangle of leaf-laden vines.
note: Whirlwind and the plane shift wording are paraphrased. A noble djinni is CR 8 with extra abilities; only the standard djinni is the summon nature's ally VII creature. The printed plane shift line details were not recorded beyond the summary above.

name: Invisible Stalker
specialQualities: natural invisibility (Su -- constant, remains invisible when attacking, not subject to invisibility purge)
improved tracking (Ex -- makes Spot checks instead of Survival to trace a creature's passage)
